title: Rapid 5-plex 3D Imaging and Single-Cell Analysis of Immune Responses in Murine Lymph Nodes
author: Boulat, Ciccarelli, et al.
materials: Timing: 2–12 days after harvesting lymph nodes

steps.title: Permeabilize and block lymph node
steps.instruction: Transfer the harvested lymph node to a new well containing 500 µL Permeabilization/Blocking Buffer and incubate on a shaker at 18 °C–25 °C for 48 h. (Optional: add anti‑mouse CD16/CD32 Fc block to the buffer if background staining is observed.)

steps.title: Incubate with primary rabbit anti‑CD21/35
steps.instruction: Prepare Antibody Cocktail 1 (rabbit anti‑CD21/35) and centrifuge it for 3 min at 10 000 × g to remove aggregates. Transfer the lymph node to a new well with 400 µL of this cocktail, cover the plate with parafilm, and incubate on a shaker at 37 °C for 48 h at 100–150 rpm.

steps.title: First wash of lymph node
steps.instruction: Transfer the node to a new well containing 500 µL Wash Buffer and incubate on a shaker at 18 °C–25 °C for 24 h, changing the buffer twice (≈8 h per wash).

steps.title: Incubate with fluorescent antibody cocktail
steps.instruction: Prepare Antibody Cocktail 2 (fluorescent antibodies against Bcl6, CD3, IgD, CD138 and secondary anti‑rabbit AF790). Centrifuge 3 min at 10 000 × g, then transfer the node to a new well with 400 µL of the cocktail, cover the plate with foil to protect from light, and incubate on a shaker at 37 °C for 96 h.

steps.title: Second wash of lymph node
steps.instruction: Transfer the node to a new well containing 500 µL Wash Buffer and incubate on a shaker at 18 °C–25 °C for 24 h, changing the buffer twice (≈8 h per wash). Samples may be stored in Wash Buffer at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare 2 % low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Make a 2 % low‑melting‑point agarose solution using a microwave, cool it to ≈37 °C, and use a Pasteur pipette to coat the bottom of a Peel‑Away embedding mold with the agarose.

steps.title: Embed lymph node in agarose
steps.instruction: Dry the lymph node on a KimWipe, place it in the agarose‑coated mold, and submerge it on a flat surface in an ice bucket. Work quickly so the agarose does not solidify before the node is fully submerged.

steps.title: Trim agarose block
steps.instruction: Trim the agarose‑embedded lymph node to a small cube oriented with its longest plane parallel to the cube sides.

substeps.instruction: Cut the embedding cube open to free the agarose block containing the node.
Using a razor blade, cut around the node to form a small cube.
Trim the cube as shown in Figure 3E, ensuring correct orientation.

steps.title: Transfer agarose cube to tube
steps.instruction: Place the agarose cube in a 15‑mL polypropylene Falcon tube (glass tubes may be used because dehydration and clearing solutions damage polystyrene).

steps.title: Dehydrate through methanol series
steps.instruction: Incubate the agarose block for 1 h each at room temperature on a shaker set to 100 rpm in the following solutions:

substeps.instruction: 50 % methanol
70 % methanol
80 % methanol
90 % methanol
100 % methanol (first change)
100 % methanol (second change)
50 % methanol – 50 % clearing solution

steps.title: Clear lymph node in BABB
steps.instruction: Transfer the block to BABB clearing solution and incubate on a shaker at 18 °C–25 °C for 12–16 h (2–3 h may be sufficient). Match incubation times across experiments to minimise differential shrinkage.

steps.title: Equilibrate in imaging solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared block to imaging solution for 5 min, then to clean imaging solution for 1 h on a shaker at 18 °C–25 °C. Perform all methanol and clearing steps in a chemical fume hood; note that the agarose may become partially opaque during dehydration. Fluorescent signal remains stable for months post‑clearing.

steps.title: Convert TIFF stack to IMS
steps.instruction: Use the Imaris File Converter to convert the acquired TIFF stack into an IMS file.

steps.title: Open image in Imaris
steps.instruction: Open the IMS file with Imaris software (version 10.1 or newer) and explore the data in 2D and 3D by toggling channels.

steps.title: Create whole lymph node surface
steps.instruction: Generate a surface representing the entire lymph node using the ‘Surface Object Creation’ wizard.

substeps.instruction: Process the whole image (no ROI), disable classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 3 (CD138‑AF647) as source, enable Smooth (20 µm grain size) and Absolute Intensity Thresholding.
Adjust threshold to segment the whole kidney‑bean‑shaped node.
Filter surfaces by volume.
Execute creation.

steps.title: Create naïve B cell surface
steps.instruction: Segment naïve B cells using the IgD‑AF700 channel.

substeps.instruction: Process whole image, no ROI, no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 4 (IgD‑AF700), Smooth (20 µm), Absolute Intensity Thresholding.
Set threshold to capture the outer ring of oblong naïve B cells; do not split surfaces.
Filter by volume.
Execute creation.

steps.title: Create T cell zone surface
steps.instruction: Segment the T cell zone using the CD3‑AF594 channel.

substeps.instruction: Process whole image, no ROI, no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 2 (CD3‑AF594), Smooth (20 µm), Absolute Intensity Thresholding.
Adjust threshold to obtain two teardrop‑shaped zones joined in the middle; do not split surfaces.
Filter by volume.
Execute creation.

steps.title: Create FDC network surface
steps.instruction: Segment follicular dendritic cell networks using the CD21/35‑AF790 channel.

substeps.instruction: Process whole image, no ROI, no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 5 (CD21‑35‑AF790), Smooth (10 µm), Absolute Intensity Thresholding.
Set threshold to isolate FDC networks that coincide with germinal centers; do not split surfaces.
Filter by volume.
Execute creation.

steps.title: Create germinal center surfaces
steps.instruction: Use machine‑learning segmentation on the IgD‑AF700 channel (with all channels) to define germinal centers.

substeps.instruction: Process whole image, no ROI, no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 4 (IgD‑AF700), Smooth (50 µm), Machine Learning Segmentation with All channels.
Paint green brush strokes inside germinal centers and pink strokes outside to train the algorithm.
Iteratively predict and refine until satisfactory across the stack.
Do not split touching objects; filter surfaces by volume.
Execute creation.
Mask the Bcl6‑AF488 channel with the germinal center surface (set voxels outside surface to 0) to generate Channel 6.

steps.title: Create plasma cell surfaces
steps.instruction: Segment plasma cells using machine‑learning on the CD138‑AF647 channel.

substeps.instruction: Process whole image, no ROI, no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 3 (CD138‑AF647), Smooth (2 µm), Machine Learning Segmentation (do not tick ‘All channels’).
Paint green strokes on plasma cells and pink strokes on background (especially outer ring).
Iteratively predict and refine until satisfactory.
Do not split touching objects; filter surfaces by volume and by mean intensity to remove artefacts.
Execute creation.

steps.title: Create follicular T cell surfaces
steps.instruction: Mask CD3‑AF594 within germinal centers, process the masked channel, and segment follicular T cells.

substeps.instruction: Mask CD3‑AF594 using the germinal center surface (set voxels outside surface to 0) to create Channel 7.
Apply Gaussian Filter = 1 to Channel 7.
Apply Baseline Subtraction (histogram) to remove non‑specific background.
In ‘Surface Object Creation’, select a region of interest (one germinal center), no classification, enable object‑object statistics.
Select Channel 7, Smooth (0.2 µm), Absolute Intensity Thresholding.
Set region of interest to representative germinal center.
Choose threshold to segment follicular T cells; enable intensity‑based surface splitting with seed point diameter 7 µm.
Filter seed points by quality, then filter surfaces by Shortest Distance to T cell zone to exclude non‑follicular T cells.
Execute creation.
Optionally classify follicular T cells by overlapping volume with the FDC surface; store parameters for batch processing.

steps.title: Export surface statistics
steps.instruction: Export all statistics for each segmented surface from Imaris and save them with consistent naming.

substeps.instruction: For each surface, open the Statistics tab, select the desired statistics, and click ‘Export all Statistics to File’.
Save the file using the surface name (e.g., “GCs”) inside a uniquely named folder for that image (e.g., “Lymph_node_1”).
Each statistic (Volume, Mean Channel Intensity, Overlapped Volume Ratio, etc.) will be saved as a separate CSV file within the folder.

steps.title: Compile statistics with custom R workflow
steps.instruction: Use the provided GitHub R pipeline to combine statistics across images.

substeps.instruction: Create an input CSV with two columns: Sample_ID (image name, e.g., Lymph_node_1) and Directory (path to the surface statistics folder, e.g., ./Lymph_node_1/GCs_Statistics).
Clone the repository: `git clone https://github.com/FrancisCrickInstitute/Imaris-3D-LN-stats` and change into the directory.
Run the compiler script with appropriate arguments: `/path/to/Rscript compiler.R <input_csv> <output_path> [classification_column]`.
The script outputs a compiled CSV containing all exported statistics for each object, together with a unique identifier for each image.
